data.name: AI Chat Conversation
data.description: Transcript of alternating turns carrying mixed rich content inline (markdown, code blocks, collapsible tool-call output) beside a resizable artifact panel that holds generated output while the stream keeps scrolling.

data.name: AI Chat Landing
data.description: Zero-state entry surface centered on a single composer with suggestion chips instead of history, sized for the moment before any content exists. The empty counterpart to a transcript.

data.name: AlertDialog — Delete
data.description: A delete button that asks the user to confirm before deleting.

data.name: AlertDialog — Loading
data.description: A confirmation dialog that shows a spinner while the action runs.

data.name: Analytics Dashboard
data.description: Three-band analytics: a row of headline tiles, then charts, then supporting tables, all re-reading from one global filter bar. Breadth over depth, a summary surface rather than a drill-down.

data.name: AppShell
data.description: A basic app shell with content padding.

data.name: AppShell — Content Only
data.description: Minimal shell with no navigation, useful for full-bleed pages, auth screens, or embedded views.

data.name: AppShell — Side Nav Only
data.description: App shell with SideNav header providing app identity, no TopNav needed.

data.name: AppShell — Top Nav Only
data.description: Simple layout with TopNav and no side navigation, suitable for landing pages.

data.name: AppShell — Top Nav with Side Nav
data.description: The most common layout with TopNav for app identity and SideNav for page-level navigation.

data.name: AppShell — With Banner
data.description: Full layout with TopNav, SideNav, and a dismissable info banner between the nav and content.

data.name: AspectRatio
data.description: Three aspect ratio containers at equal height (1:1, 4:3, and 16:9), each showing an image with its ratio labeled below.

data.name: AspectRatio — 16:9 Widescreen Image
data.description: 16:9 widescreen aspect ratio wrapping an image.

data.name: AspectRatio — Circle Image
data.description: Circular container via shape="ellipse" with ratio={1}, ideal for avatars and profile images.

data.name: AspectRatio — Image Gallery
data.description: Grid of images with consistent 4:3 aspect ratios.

data.name: AspectRatio — Loading Skeleton
data.description: Aspect ratio container with a skeleton loading placeholder.

data.name: AspectRatio — Square Image
data.description: 1:1 square aspect ratio, ideal for avatars and Instagram-style images.

data.name: Avatar
data.description: Avatars at every size with an image, initials fallback, and a status dot. A quick visual reference for choosing the right size.

data.name: Avatar — Fallback Chain
data.description: Demonstrates the avatar fallback chain: primary image, fallback image, initials, then default icon.

data.name: Avatar — Group
data.description: Overlap multiple avatars in a row to represent a group of people. Use for team lists, PR reviewers, or participant counts where you want to show faces without taking up much space.

data.name: Avatar — Initials
data.description: Show initials instead of a photo. The avatar extracts the first and last initials from the name automatically. Use when you only have a user name, like in anonymous accounts or new user onboarding.

data.name: Avatar — Interactive
data.description: Make an avatar interactive by passing `href` to render it as a link or `onClick` to render it as a button. Both forms are focusable and show a focus-visible ring for keyboard users. Use for profile links, mention pop-ups, or any avatar people can act on.

data.name: Avatar — Photo
data.description: Show a profile photo at different sizes. Use when you have a user photo URL. If the image fails to load, initials are shown instead.

data.name: Avatar — Status Dot
data.description: Add a status dot to an avatar to show whether someone is online, away, or busy. Use in chat, messaging, or any UI where knowing availability matters.

data.name: Avatar — Tooltip
data.description: By default an avatar shows its name in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. Pass a string to show custom text instead, or false to turn the tooltip off.

data.name: Avatar — User Card
data.description: Place an avatar next to a name and role to create a user card row. Use for comment headers, contact lists, profile sections, or anywhere you need to identify a person at a glance.

data.name: AvatarGroup
data.description: Overlapping avatar rows with a sliced visible set and a server-side overflow count. Shows team members in a compact facepile layout.

data.name: AvatarGroup — Interactive
data.description: A facepile whose avatars link to profiles, with an overflow indicator that opens the full member list. The whole group is one Tab stop; arrow keys move between the avatars and the overflow button.

data.name: AvatarGroupOverflow
data.description: Overflow indicators for hidden avatars, including the default +N label and custom count text.

data.name: AvatarGroupOverflow — Custom Text
data.description: Provide short custom children such as 12+ when the overflow count needs compact product-specific formatting.

data.name: AvatarGroupOverflow — Default Count
data.description: Use AvatarGroupOverflow without children to render the standard +N overflow count.

data.name: AvatarStatusDot
data.description: AvatarStatusDot renders a presence indicator on an Avatar, with variants for positive, neutral, and negative states. The dot size automatically coordinates with the Avatar size.

data.name: AvatarStatusDot — Variants
data.description: Presence dots on Avatars using the success, neutral, and error variants. Pass an AvatarStatusDot to the Avatar status prop; the dot sizes itself to match the Avatar.

data.name: Badge — Colors
data.description: Tag items with color-coded categories like teams, priorities, or topics. Use the 9 non-semantic color variants when you need to distinguish groups visually.

data.name: Badge — Counts
data.description: Show a number inside a badge for notification counts, unread messages, or task totals. Use next to icons, nav items, or list labels.

data.name: Badge — Status
data.description: Show the state of an item like Active, Pending, or Failed. Use in table rows, list items, or detail pages where users need to see status at a glance.

data.name: Badge — Variants
data.description: All semantic and color badge variants in a single view. Use semantic variants for status and color variants for categories.

data.name: Banner — Action
data.description: Add a button to a banner so the user can act on the message. Use for trial expirations, payment failures, or anything that needs a response.

data.name: Banner — Collapsible
data.description: Combine an action button, dismiss control, and a collapsible detail area in one banner. Children sit behind the toggle by default; `collapsible={{defaultIsOpen: true}}` starts it open, and `collapsible={false}` drops the toggle entirely. Use for complex notifications like config changes or deployment summaries.

data.name: Banner — Dismiss
data.description: Let the user close a banner after reading it. Use for maintenance notices, feature tips, or any non-critical message the user can acknowledge.

data.name: Banner — Floating
data.description: A floating banner raised with `elevation="med"`. Banners are inline by default; raise one when it should read as an overlay above content.

data.name: Banner — Full Width
data.description: A full-width banner with no border radius for page-level notifications. Use at the top of a page for site-wide announcements or maintenance alerts.

data.name: Banner — Statuses
data.description: All four status banners stacked: info, success, warning, and error. A quick visual reference for choosing the right status.

data.name: Banner — Statuses
data.description: All 4 banner statuses: info, success, warning, and error. Use to show persistent messages like updates, confirmations, cautions, or problems at the top of a page or section.

data.name: BaseTypeahead
data.description: A custom result renderer that adds supporting metadata while BaseTypeahead retains option semantics and keyboard behavior.

data.name: BaseTypeahead — Custom Search Bar
data.description: BaseTypeahead embedded inside a custom-styled wrapper. The wrapper provides its own border and icon chrome; anchorRef positions the dropdown relative to it. Use this pattern when Typeahead's built-in field layout does not fit your composition.

data.name: Basic
data.description: Open a modal drawer from a single trigger. The scrim dims the page; Escape, a scrim click, or the header close button closes it, and focus returns to the trigger.

data.name: Basic Login
data.description: Minimal centered credential form on a plain ground: two fields and a submit, nothing competing for attention. The least-chrome entry surface.

data.name: Blank
data.description: Bare scaffold: one heading slot, one empty content region, no navigation and no chrome. The starting point when every other layout imposes more structure than wanted.

data.name: Blockquote — Showcase
data.description: Blockquote with and without citation. A quick visual reference for the blockquote component.

data.name: Blockquote — Testimonials
data.description: Multiple quotes arranged in a card grid for a testimonials section. Combine with Card and Grid to create social-proof layouts.

data.name: Blockquote — With Attribution
data.description: A plain quote and a quote with a cite attribution. Use cite to credit the original author or source.

data.name: Bottom Sheet
data.description: A mobile filter surface that rises from the bottom edge.

data.name: Bottom Sheet — Height variants
data.description: Compares hug, capped, and tall starting heights for different amounts of content.

data.name: Bottom Sheet — Mobile keyboard
data.description: Uses a tall, scrollable form that keeps focused controls visible above the mobile keyboard.

data.name: Bottom Sheet — Multi-step flow
data.description: A three-step flow of standalone sheets of different heights, driven by one state value: moving on replaces the open step in place. This is the replacement for the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher.

data.name: Bottom Sheet — No scrim
data.description: Keeps the page visible and interactive behind a non-modal bottom sheet.

data.name: Bottom Sheet — Review flow
data.description: A two-step form flow of two standalone sheets driven by one state value: Continue replaces the review step with the confirmation in place, and Back returns.

data.name: Bottom Sheet — Snap points
data.description: Drag-to-resize stops: a half-height working surface, and a peek that slides away and thins the scrim.

data.name: BreadcrumbItem
data.description: BreadcrumbItem represents a single step in a breadcrumb trail, supporting links, icons, current-page markers, and custom link components.

data.name: BreadcrumbItem — Basic
data.description: Breadcrumb links inside a Breadcrumbs trail. Ancestor pages get an href; mark the last item with isCurrent to render it as plain text for the current page.

data.name: Breadcrumbs
data.description: A breadcrumb trail showing page hierarchy with linked ancestors and a current page.

data.name: Breadcrumbs — Deep Path
data.description: A 5-level breadcrumb trail for deeply nested content. Use in e-commerce, file browsers, or any UI with several levels of hierarchy.

data.name: Breadcrumbs — Icons
data.description: Add icons before breadcrumb labels for quick recognition. Use a home icon on the root item and contextual icons on key sections.

data.name: Breadcrumbs — Menu item
data.description: Give a mid-trail crumb a `menu` prop to turn it into a menu trigger for switching between sibling destinations. It reuses the same item API as DropdownMenu, so an existing option array (or composed item children) drops in verbatim.

data.name: Breadcrumbs — Separators
data.description: Swap the default "/" for a different character like chevrons, arrows, or dots. Use when the visual style of the page calls for a different separator.

data.name: Breadcrumbs — Variants
data.description: Compare the default and supporting variants side by side. Use the supporting variant in dense UIs like admin panels where the breadcrumb should be subtle.

data.name: Button — End Slot
data.description: Buttons with a trailing badge showing a count or status. Use for notification counts, unread messages, or any button that needs a visual indicator.

data.name: Button — Floating
data.description: A floating action button raised with `elevation="med"`. Use elevation for buttons that hover above content, like a FAB.

data.name: Button — Icon
data.description: Buttons with a leading icon that reinforces the label. Use when the icon helps the user identify the action faster, like a plus for "New" or a trash can for "Delete".

data.name: Button — Sizes
data.description: Small, medium, and large buttons side by side. Use small in dense UIs like toolbars, medium for most cases, and large for prominent CTAs.

data.name: Button — Variants
data.description: All four button variants side by side: primary, secondary, ghost, and destructive. A quick visual reference for choosing the right variant.

data.name: Button — Variants
data.description: All 4 button variants in default, disabled, and loading states. Use primary for the main action, secondary for most others, ghost for low-emphasis, and destructive for dangerous actions.

data.name: ButtonGroup — Basic
data.description: Three related actions joined into a single connected control. Provide a group label for accessibility and keep all buttons the same variant so they read as one unit.

data.name: ButtonGroup — Floating
data.description: A grouped action bar raised with `elevation="med"`. The connected buttons share one surface, so the shadow lifts them as a unit.

data.name: Calendar
data.description: An interactive single-date calendar with a selected date. Click any day to change the selection.

data.name: Calendar — Constraints
data.description: Limit which dates can be selected using min/max bounds and custom rules like weekdays only. Use for scheduling UIs where certain dates are unavailable.

data.name: Calendar — Range
data.description: Pick a start and end date with the range highlighted between them. Use for booking dates, time-off requests, or report filters.

data.name: Calendar — Single
data.description: Pick one date from a month grid. Use for appointment dates, due dates, or any field that needs a single date.

data.name: Calendar — Two Months
data.description: Two months side by side for selecting ranges that span a month boundary. Use in booking or travel UIs where check-in and check-out often fall in different months.

data.name: Canvas Editor
data.description: Layered artboard workspace: document tabs over a layer rail, a fixed-size frame you zoom on a muted backdrop, and an inspector of position, type, and filter fields that retargets to the selected layer. Objects hold a coordinate rather than reflowing, so moving one never moves another.

data.name: Card
data.description: A card with a heading and body text showing the default container style.

data.name: Card — Callout
data.description: Muted-variant cards for tips, notes, or supplementary information. Use when content should be visually distinct but not prominent. The muted variant uses a wash background instead of the elevated default, making it feel recessed rather than raised. Works well in sidebars, help panels, or inline callouts.

data.name: Card — Elevations
data.description: The four elevation levels side by side. Cards are flat by default; raise a card with `elevation` only when it needs to float above surrounding content.

data.name: Card — Layout
data.description: A card with a structured header, content area, and footer with action buttons. Use for forms, dialogs, or settings panels that need clear sections. Pair Card with Layout to get automatic dividers between header, content, and footer. The footer aligns actions to the right by default.

data.name: Card — Simple
data.description: A card with a heading and body text. Use for summaries, descriptions, or any grouped content that needs visual separation from the page. The card handles its own border, background, and padding; just pass your content as children. Set a width to constrain it, or leave it to fill the parent.

data.name: Card — Variants
data.description: Default, muted, and color variants side by side. Use color variants to categorize cards visually, like team colors, project tags, or content types. Each color uses the corresponding background token from the theme, so they adapt to light and dark mode automatically.

data.name: Card Grid
data.description: Searchable, browsable card grid with filter tabs and a real empty state: uniform tiles organized by topic, narrowing in place, with no detail surface behind them.

data.name: Carousel
data.description: A horizontal carousel of cards with scroll-snap and navigation buttons. Scroll or click the arrows to browse.

data.name: Carousel — Cards
data.description: A horizontally scrollable row of cards with snap scrolling enabled. Use for feature grids, product lists, or any set of cards that overflows the available width. The carousel adds fade edges and navigation buttons automatically.

data.name: Carousel — Snap
data.description: Scroll-snap carousel with navigation buttons and team member cards. Each card snaps to the start edge on scroll. Use when items should be viewed one at a time rather than as a continuous strip.

data.name: Center
data.description: Content centered horizontally and vertically inside a fixed-height container.

data.name: Center — Horizontal Center
data.description: A formatting control group centered with axis="horizontal" in the default horizontal writing mode. In other writing modes, Center currently follows the flex main axis rather than guaranteeing physical horizontal centering.

data.name: Center — Vertical & Horizontal Center
data.description: An empty state with an icon, heading, and description centered both vertically and horizontally inside a card. This is the most common use of Center: placing content in the middle of a fixed-height area like a panel, card, or content region. The height prop defines the centering space.

data.name: Centered Hero
data.description: Symmetrical centered stack (headline, short blurb, paired call-to-action buttons) resting on one wide full-bleed picture, with nothing on either flank competing.

data.name: ChatComposer — Attachments
data.description: Chat composer with removable file tokens in a collapsible drawer. Use when users can attach files or context to their message.

data.name: ChatComposer — Flat
data.description: The composer is raised by default (`elevation="low"`). Set `elevation="none"` to flatten it; it then draws a border with the same rest / hover / focus treatment as a text input.

data.name: ChatComposer — Footer Actions
data.description: Chat composer with dropdown menus for a model selector and settings in the footer, and a mic button in the send actions slot.

data.name: ChatComposer — Full Featured
data.description: Chat composer with all slots populated: collapsible attachment drawer, header actions, context progress bar, footer dropdown menus, and mic button. Shows the maximum composer configuration.

data.name: ChatComposer — Simple
data.description: Minimal chat composer with a placeholder and submit handler. The simplest way to drop a message input into a page.

data.name: ChatComposer — Streaming
data.description: Chat composer with streaming state and a stop button. Use when the assistant is generating a response and the user can cancel.

data.name: ChatComposer — Validation
data.description: Chat composer with error and warning status messages. Status can appear above or below the composer to surface validation or system feedback.

data.name: ChatComposerDrawer
data.description: Composer drawer with file tokens, a collapsible toggle, and header actions. Use as a starting point for any chat composer with attachments.

data.name: ChatComposerDrawer — Attachments
data.description: Drawer with two rows: a scrollable carousel of image thumbnails and a row of removable file tokens. Omit count to keep the drawer always expanded.

data.name: ChatComposerDrawer — Collapsible
data.description: Drawer with many items and a collapse toggle. Pass count to enable the toggle; collapsed state shows a badge with the total count and a label.

data.name: ChatComposerDrawer — Feedback
data.description: Chat composer drawer with a feedback prompt and selectable lettered options. Use for user confirmation workflows that require explicit action before proceeding.

data.name: ChatComposerDrawer — With Progress
data.description: Drawer paired with a context progress bar in the header. Show context window usage when attachments consume part of the available token budget.

data.name: ChatComposerInput — Controlled
data.description: Controlled chat input with live value display. Use controlled mode when you need to read or transform the input value outside the composer.

data.name: ChatComposerInput — Disabled
data.description: Composer in a disabled state. Use when the input should be visible but not interactive, such as during streaming or when a prerequisite is unmet.

data.name: ChatComposerInput — Mentions
data.description: Chat input with an @ trigger that opens a typeahead menu for mentioning users. Selected names appear as inline tokens.

data.name: ChatComposerInput — Multiple Triggers
data.description: Chat input with both @ mentions and / commands. Each trigger type renders tokens in a distinct color so users can tell them apart at a glance.

data.name: ChatComposerInput — Slash Commands
data.description: Chat input with a / trigger for command selection. Use for AI assistants or bots that support structured commands.

data.name: ChatDictationButton
data.description: Interactive dictation button connected to the SpeechRecognition API via useChatDictation. Click the mic to dictate into the composer.

data.name: ChatDictationButton — Basic
data.description: A dictation button wired to useChatDictation and placed in the sendActions slot of a ChatComposer. Click the microphone to transcribe speech into the input.

data.name: ChatDictationButton — In Composer
data.description: Dictation button placed in the sendActions slot of a chat composer. Shows the recommended integration point for voice input alongside the send button.

data.name: ChatDictationButton — Sizes
data.description: Small and medium dictation buttons side by side. Use small in compact composer densities and medium for standard layouts.

data.name: ChatDictationButton — States
data.description: Dictation button in idle, listening, and speaking states side by side. Shows the three visual phases of a voice input interaction.

data.name: ChatLayout — Panel View
data.description: Narrow sidebar chat in a constrained container that triggers compact density. Use for side panels, drawers, or embedded chat widgets where horizontal space is limited.

data.name: ChatLayoutScrollButton
data.description: Scroll button in hidden, visible, and expanded (with label) states. The button fades in when the user scrolls up and expands when new messages arrive.

data.name: ChatLayoutScrollButton — Labels
data.description: Scroll button with different labels for context-specific notifications like new messages, unread replies, or a generic scroll prompt.

data.name: ChatMessage
data.description: A user multi-bubble group with delivery status and an assistant ghost response with avatar, name, timestamp, and model info.

data.name: ChatMessage — Avatar & Name
data.description: Messages with avatars and sender names. Place the name on the bubble when using bubbles, or on the message wrapper for raw content.

data.name: ChatMessage — Ghost
data.description: Ghost variant for messages without visible bubble boundaries. Keeps padding for alignment but renders a transparent background, useful for AI-style responses.

data.name: ChatMessage — Multi-Bubble
data.description: Grouped bubbles using the group prop for corner radius reduction. Use first, middle, and last to visually connect related bubbles from the same sender.

data.name: ChatMessageBubble
data.description: Grouped user bubbles with filled styling and a ghost-variant agent response, with timestamps and delivery status.

data.name: ChatMessageBubble — Custom Content
data.description: Custom in-message content aligned to the bubble text column. An artifact card is wrapped in a ghost bubble with width="100%", so its left edge matches the bubble text and it spans the full message column instead of the default bubble width cap; the timestamp rides the bubble metadata slot.

data.name: ChatMessageBubble — Density
data.description: Compact, balanced, and spacious density modes side by side. Density controls bubble padding, corner radius, and spacing between grouped bubbles.

data.name: ChatMessageBubble — Grouping
data.description: Multi-bubble messages using first, middle, and last group positions. Grouped bubbles tighten corner radius on the sender side for a continuous visual flow.

data.name: ChatMessageBubble — Metadata
data.description: Bubbles with name and metadata slots aligned to bubble padding. Put name on the first bubble and metadata on the last bubble in a message.

data.name: ChatMessageBubble — Variants
data.description: Filled and ghost bubble variants for both user and assistant senders. Use filled for standard messages and ghost when content needs alignment without a visual boundary.

data.name: ChatMessageList
data.description: Basic AI chat conversation with user and assistant messages. The simplest way to render a message list with alternating sender bubbles, metadata, and a date divider.

data.name: ChatMessageList — Density
data.description: Side-by-side comparison of compact, balanced, and spacious densities. Use compact in sidebars or panels, balanced for most full-page chat, and spacious for long-form reading. Use gap when row spacing needs to differ from density.

data.name: ChatMessageList — Full Featured
data.description: Conversation showcasing system messages, multi-bubble grouping, markdown, code blocks, and metadata. Combines date dividers, ghost bubbles, grouped messages, and rich content in a single example.

data.name: ChatMessageMetadata
data.description: Three-message conversation showcasing error status with retry, delivery status, and full footer actions with model label.

data.name: ChatMessageMetadata — Footer Actions
data.description: Assistant message with footer actions: copy, retry, thumbs up/down, and model label. Use for AI responses that need feedback or utility controls.

data.name: ChatMessageMetadata — Status
data.description: All 5 delivery statuses (sending, sent, delivered, read, and error), each with a timestamp. Use to show message delivery progress or surface failures.

data.name: ChatMessageMetadata — Timestamps
data.description: Timestamp-only metadata on user and assistant messages. Supports absolute time and relative formats via Timestamp.

data.name: ChatSendButton
data.description: Ready, custom icon, and streaming states of the send button.

data.name: ChatSendButton — Custom Icon
data.description: Send buttons with custom icons via sendIcon and stopIcon props. Use to match the personality of the chat experience: a paper airplane for messaging, sparkles for AI generation, or a check mark for confirmation flows.

data.name: ChatSendButton — In Composer
data.description: Send button inside ChatComposer, where it reads state from context automatically. No wiring needed; the button enables when the input has content.

data.name: ChatSendButton — States
data.description: Disabled, ready, and streaming states at both sizes. The button automatically toggles between send (primary) and stop (secondary) based on streaming state.

data.name: ChatSystemMessage
data.description: System messages for date dividers, status updates, and informational notices. Shows both default and divider variants in a realistic conversation flow.

data.name: ChatSystemMessage — Icon
data.description: System messages with a leading icon that reinforces the message type. Use icons to help users scan and identify message categories at a glance.

data.name: ChatSystemMessage — Status Updates
data.description: Realistic status messages in a conversation flow showing membership changes, timestamps, and resolution notices.

data.name: ChatSystemMessage — Variants
data.description: Default and divider variants side by side. Use default for inline status updates and divider for date separators or section breaks.

data.name: ChatTokenizedText — Basic
data.description: A message with @mention tokens. Each matching pattern is replaced with its display name badge.

data.name: ChatTokenizedText — Colors
data.description: Tokens with different color variants to distinguish mentions, bugs, and features. Use variant colors to create a visual taxonomy: blue for people, red for bugs, green for features.

data.name: ChatToolCalls — Expandable
data.description: Tool calls with expandable result details showing diffs and command output in code blocks. Click a row to reveal its result.

data.name: ChatToolCalls — Simple
data.description: A single inline tool call above a collapsible multi-call group with diff stats. Shows both layouts side by side.

data.name: ChatToolCalls — Statuses
data.description: All four status states (pending, running, complete, and error) shown together in a single group.

data.name: CheckboxInput
data.description: Interactive checkboxes showing checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states with descriptions.

data.name: CheckboxInput — Indeterminate
data.description: A "select all" checkbox that controls a group of options. When only some options are checked, it shows a dash instead of a checkmark. Clicking it checks or unchecks everything.

data.name: CheckboxInput — States
data.description: Checkboxes with labels and descriptions in checked, unchecked, and disabled states. Each checkbox controls a single on/off setting. Add a description to explain what the setting does.

data.name: CheckboxInput — Status
data.description: Checkboxes with error, warning, and success validation messages. Use the status prop to show feedback after form validation: errors block submission, warnings inform, and success confirms.

data.name: CheckboxList — Select All With Indeterminate
data.description: A "select all" toggle at the top of a checkbox list that switches to an indeterminate dash when only some items are checked, useful for bulk actions like exporting documents or assigning permissions where users often want everything at once.

data.name: CheckboxList — With End Content
data.description: Badges in the trailing slot show contextual info, like a price or status, next to each option without cluttering the label, so users can compare choices at a glance.

data.name: CheckboxListItem
data.description: Checkbox list items with labels, descriptions, and different states including disabled.

data.name: CheckboxListItem — Basic
data.description: Checkbox items with labels and descriptions inside a controlled CheckboxList. Use for multi-select option groups like notification preferences.

data.name: Checkout Form
data.description: Long sectioned form running beside a summary that stays visible while the fields scroll and recalculates as they change, ending on a terminal confirm of the total. Sections run contact, address, delivery choice, then card details.

data.name: Checkout Wizard
data.description: Multi-step checkout, cart, order, and payment wizard with a running summary that recalculates as answers change. It adapts to its host width, renders the summary first on narrow surfaces, validates every forward path, and completes locally without sending payment.

data.name: Citation — Inline Text
data.description: Citations embedded within a paragraph of text, showing how they flow inline with surrounding content.

data.name: Citation — Showcase
data.description: All citation variants at a glance: label chips and numbered badges, with and without icons and links.

data.name: Citation — Source List
data.description: A list of citation sources with icons, as you might show at the end of an AI-generated response or article footer.

data.name: Classic Gallery
data.description: Uniform grid of equal-ratio media tiles under a centered intro, with filter tabs that narrow the set in place. Regular rhythm, unlike the variable-height masonry variant.

data.name: ClickableCard
data.description: A clickable card that navigates on click. Nested interactive elements work independently.

data.name: ClickableCard — Elevated
data.description: A clickable card raised with `elevation="med"` so the shadow signals the whole surface is interactive.

data.name: ClickableCardWithNestedButton
data.description: A product card that navigates on click but has an independent "Add to cart" button inside.

data.name: Code
data.description: Inline code snippets inside a sentence showing how Code renders alongside body text.

data.name: Code — Config
data.description: A JSON configuration file with a title bar and line numbers. The title prop adds a filename label in the header so readers know which file the code belongs to.

data.name: Code — Content Types
data.description: Inline code used for variables, terminal commands, CSS properties, file paths, and keyboard shortcuts. Shows how Code adapts to different kinds of technical content.

data.name: Code — Highlighted
data.description: TypeScript code with specific lines highlighted to draw attention to a key section. Use highlightLines to call out new or important code in tutorials and changelogs.

data.name: Code — Inline
data.description: Inline code references mixed within a paragraph of body text. Use Code to mark up function names, hooks, or API terms so they stand out from surrounding prose.

data.name: Code — Scrollable
data.description: A long code block with a max height that enables vertical scrolling. Use maxHeight to keep the block from dominating the page when displaying large files.

data.name: Code — Snippet
data.description: Short terminal commands with no header: the copy button sits in its own column beside the code, so a one-line command reads as a single row and a long line ends before the button instead of running under it. Use for install instructions or one-liner commands that readers will paste directly.

data.name: Code — Terminal
data.description: A dark terminal-style command block: a bash CodeBlock wrapped in SyntaxTheme with the GitHub Dark preset, copy button on, and no line numbers. Use for shell sessions or CLI output that should read as a terminal even on light pages. Reach for a dark syntax preset instead of hand-rolling a dark box with custom CSS.

data.name: Code — Text Sizes
data.description: Inline code rendered inside heading, body, supporting, and label text. Code automatically matches the font size of its parent text element.

data.name: CodeBlock
data.description: A syntax-highlighted TypeScript code block with line numbers, a title bar, and a copy button.

data.name: Collapsible
data.description: An accordion group with three collapsible sections in single mode: opening one closes the others.

data.name: Collapsible — Controlled
data.description: Manage the open section from parent state, so something other than a click can move it: a URL parameter, a form jumping to the step that failed validation, or the Previous/Next controls shown here. onChange hands back the whole open value.

data.name: Collapsible — FAQ
data.description: FAQ built with hasDividers: row hairlines and density padding with no custom CSS. Questions set their own type — body at semibold, not the trigger's default 17px large — so a list of questions reads as rows rather than a stack of headings, and question and answer separate on weight and color instead of size.

data.name: Collapsible — Multiple Mode
data.description: Several sections open at once, for comparing across them — feature lists, pricing tiers. One Collapsible per Card, so each trigger keeps its own large type: it is the heading of its surface, not a row in a list.

data.name: Collapsible — Single Mode
data.description: Only one section open at a time, so a single body of content competes for attention. Use defaultValue to pre-expand whichever section a first-time reader needs. Each Collapsible owns a Section, so its trigger is that section heading.

data.name: Collapsible — With Dividers
data.description: A flat list on the page background with hand-placed Dividers, for detail panels and sidebars where cards would add too much weight. Rows, so the triggers step down to body-semibold and a supporting metadata line sits under each answer.

data.name: Collapsible Table
data.description: Several tables on one page, each in a collapsible card with its own columns — for groups that do not share a schema, where one table would stand full of empty cells. One time range drives them all, and rows expand into a history chart. Accounts, integrations, sections, sort, expand, or collapse.

data.name: CollapsibleGroup
data.description: CollapsibleGroup coordinates its Collapsible children: with type="single", opening one closes the others. No state or handlers in the example — the group owns which value is open and each child only declares its own. One Collapsible per Card, so each trigger keeps its default large type as the heading of its own surface.

data.name: CollapsibleGroup — Density
data.description: density sets the block padding on every row in the group, so a list of sections can be tuned to the surface it sits on without touching the rows. compact for dense surfaces like sidebars and inspectors, balanced (the default) for page content, spacious for a short list that is the main thing on the page. It follows Table's scale and pairs with hasDividers, which turns it on at balanced.

data.name: CommandPalette — Async Search

data.name: CommandPaletteGroup

data.name: CommandPaletteGroup — Basic

data.name: CommandPaletteItem — Basic
data.description: Selectable command palette items inside a CommandPaletteList, including highlighted and disabled states. Use when composing a palette manually instead of a search source.

data.description: Scrollable command palette list with grouped items, including a highlighted item, composed without a full CommandPalette.

data.description: Flat list showing the highlighted, selected, and disabled item states. Use CommandPaletteGroup to add section headings.

data.name: Comparison Table
data.description: Transposed matrix that puts candidates in the columns and criteria in grouped rows, with a pinned label column that survives horizontal scroll, columns you can swap or add, and best-in-row marks you can toggle. Compare, comparison, matrix, spec sheet, feature grid, pricing table, benchmark, frozen column, sticky column, or side-by-side.

data.description: A multi-step deadline field: pick a preset like Today or Next week, or switch to a custom date and time before applying. The popup stays open until the user commits, so the content owns the Apply action.

data.name: ComplexSelector — Tree Search
data.description: A destination picker that combines a search field with a TreeList hierarchy. TreeList owns tree keyboard navigation; ComplexSelector owns the trigger, popover, and focus restore. Selecting a folder closes the popup.

data.name: Contact Form
data.description: Flat single-column form mixing control types (text, pill toggles, dropdowns, long free-text) landing on one full-width submit. No steps, no branching, no summary rail.

data.name: ContextMenu
data.description: An adaptive context area that supports long-press on compact touch screens and right-click elsewhere.

data.name: ContextMenu — Basic
data.description: An adaptive context area: long-press opens a BottomSheet on compact touch screens, while right-click opens a cursor-positioned menu elsewhere.

data.name: ContextMenu — Bottom Sheet
data.description: A ContextMenu using the explicit BottomSheet presentation. Long-press the target on touch devices or right-click it with a pointer. Keep a visible menu trigger for important mobile actions.

data.name: ContextMenuItem
data.description: Context menu with custom-rendered items using ContextMenuItem for icons and descriptions.

data.name: ContextMenuItem — Basic
data.description: Context menu items with labels and secondary descriptions. Use ContextMenuItem to render custom menu entries with consistent styling.

data.name: createAnimator — Playing cards in plain JavaScript
data.description: The playing card from the useAnimator example, built in plain JavaScript with createAnimator and pointer events: it follows a drag, springs back on a gentle release, flies off with momentum on a quick flick, and a button discards it from the keyboard. React only mounts it.

data.name: createDragToSnapPoints — Playing card in plain JavaScript
data.description: The three-place playing card from the useDragToSnapPoints example, built in plain JavaScript with createDragToSnapPoints: a sideways drag settles it on the nearest place or the next after a flick, buttons settle it from the keyboard, and a live region announces the place. React only mounts it.

data.name: Data Dashboard
data.description: Comparison-heavy analytics behind a persistent filter bar: tiles that each carry an inline sparkline and several period-over-period deltas, then segmented breakdowns underneath. Every number is shown against another number.

data.name: DateInput
data.description: A date input field with a calendar popover. Type a date or click the calendar icon to pick one.

data.name: DateInput — Clearable
data.description: Date input with a clear button that resets the value. Use when the date field is optional and the user may need to undo their selection.

data.name: DateInput — Description
data.description: Date input with helper text below the label explaining what the field expects. Use when the purpose of the date is not obvious from the label alone.

data.name: DateInput — Formats
data.description: The format prop reuses Timestamp's format vocabulary to control how the committed value is displayed: date, date_long (default), date_weekday, and system_date, or a function for a fully custom string. Formatting applies only to the committed value, never to text the user is actively typing.

data.name: DateInput — Min/Max Constraints
data.description: Date input constrained to a min/max window. Use when only certain dates are valid, like booking availability or a fiscal quarter.

data.name: DateInput — Validation
data.description: Date input in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface validation issues, caution the user, or confirm a valid selection.

data.name: DateRangeInput
data.description: A date range picker with a button trigger and dual-month calendar popover with preset ranges.

data.name: DateRangeInput — Validation
data.description: Date range input in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface booking conflicts, flag high-demand periods, or confirm an available range.

data.name: DateRangeInput — With Presets
data.description: Date range picker with quick-select presets for common periods. Use for analytics dashboards, report filters, or any context where users frequently select standard time windows.

data.name: DateTimeInput
data.description: A combined date and time picker. Desktop opens a calendar popover with a time input; touch devices open a Date/Time bottom sheet.

data.name: DateTimeInput — Validation
data.description: DateTimeInput in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface scheduling conflicts, caution the user about edge cases, or confirm a valid datetime.

data.name: Dialog
data.description: Modal dialog with a header, body content, and close button.

data.name: Dialog — Adaptive presentation
data.description: Opt-in recipe for an AdaptiveDialog wrapper: Dialog remains the default everywhere, while touchPresentation="bottom-sheet" switches only at lg and below when pointer is coarse and hover is unavailable. Includes a deterministic presentation override for tests/unusual environments and notes that BottomSheet purpose controls swipe and scrim dismissal. Usage examples: touchPresentation="dialog" keeps Dialog, "fullscreen" chooses fullscreen Dialog, and "bottom-sheet" chooses BottomSheet only for the touch-oriented range. Keep presentation as the deterministic override. Do not use this by default for AlertDialog or destructive confirmations.

data.name: Dialog — Confirmation
data.description: Asks the user to confirm a destructive action before it happens. Use before deleting projects, removing team members, revoking API keys, or any irreversible operation.

data.name: Dialog — Form
data.description: Collects user input without navigating away from the page. Uses purpose="form" so clicking the backdrop won't close it. Use for editing profiles, creating items, or updating settings inline.

data.name: Dialog — Fullscreen
data.description: Takes over the entire viewport for content that needs maximum space. Use for documentation viewers, rich text editors, multi-step wizards, or media previews where the standard dialog width is too narrow.

data.name: Dialog — Required
data.description: Cannot be dismissed by Escape or backdrop click; the user must explicitly choose an action. Uses purpose="required". Use for ownership transfers, legal acknowledgements, or critical decisions where skipping is not an option.

data.name: Dialog — Scrollable
data.description: Constrains the dialog height and scrolls the body when content overflows. Use for terms and conditions, license agreements, changelogs, or any long-form content the user needs to review before accepting.

data.name: Dialog Wizard
data.description: Step through a short flow in a dialog, overlay, or popup launched from the page underneath, which stays where it was. Compact step markers and a pinned action row inside a constrained width, rather than the full page a wizard usually gets. Best for two to four short steps — setup, invite, schedule, onboarding — where losing the context underneath would cost more than the flow is worth.

data.name: DialogHeader
data.description: DialogHeader provides a structured header for dialogs with slots for title, subtitle, close button, and optional start or end content.

data.name: DialogHeader — Basic
data.description: A DialogHeader with a title, subtitle, and close button, placed in the header slot of a Dialog Layout. Pass onOpenChange to render the close button.

data.name: Divider — Full Bleed
data.description: Divider that extends past container padding to span the full width. Use inside cards or panels when you want a clean edge-to-edge separation, like between an order summary and total.

data.name: Divider — Variants
data.description: Horizontal dividers in subtle and strong variants, plus a labeled divider. A quick visual reference for separator styles.

data.name: Divider — Variants
data.description: Subtle, labeled, and strong dividers in a single card. Use subtle between related sections, labeled for alternatives like "or", and strong for high-contrast boundaries.

data.name: Divider — Vertical
data.description: Vertical dividers separating side-by-side metrics. Use between stat cards, toolbar groups, or any horizontal layout where you need a visual boundary between sections.

data.name: Documentation Catalog

data.name: Documentation Design
data.description: Reference article alternating prose with live rendered examples: an interactive preview, a property table, paired do and don't comparisons, and copyable code blocks.

data.name: Documentation Technical
data.description: Reference article ordered as sequential numbered steps with code at each stage, plus callout cards for prerequisites and onward links. A linear walkthrough rather than a browsable reference.

data.name: DrawerHeader
data.description: DrawerHeader provides a structured header for drawers with slots for title, subtitle, close button, and optional start or end content.

data.name: DropdownMenu
data.description: A button that opens a dropdown menu with action items. The menu starts open for preview.

data.name: DropdownMenu — Actions
data.description: Action menu with dividers separating safe and destructive operations. Use for row-level actions on items like documents, projects, or records.

data.name: DropdownMenu — Adaptive presentation
data.description: Chooses a bottom sheet for compact touch surfaces and an anchored popover otherwise. The media query is product policy, while DropdownMenu owns both presentations.

data.name: DropdownMenu — Disabled
data.description: Menu with selectively disabled items based on permissions. Use when some actions require higher privileges, like admin-only operations.

data.name: DropdownMenu — Icon Trigger
data.description: Overflow menu triggered by an icon-only button with no chevron or label text. Use for row-level actions in tables, cards, or lists where a text button would take too much space.

data.name: DropdownMenu — Sections
data.description: Menu items organized into titled sections for easy scanning. Use when you have 6+ actions that fall into distinct categories, like Create vs Manage.

data.name: DropdownMenu — Submenu
data.description: Action menu with a nested submenu. Hover or Right arrow opens the flyout; Left arrow / Escape closes it. Use to group related destinations or secondary actions without crowding the top level.

data.name: DropdownMenuGroup
data.description: A compound-mode menu whose rows are titled in groups. Each DropdownMenuGroup renders a role="group" named by its heading; arrow keys and typeahead skip the heading.

data.name: DropdownMenuGroup — Selectable rows
data.description: Titled groups around a radio group and checkbox rows — the rows the data API cannot express, which is why the heading lives in compound mode.

data.name: DropdownMenuItem
data.description: Dropdown menu with custom-rendered items using DropdownMenuItem for icons and descriptions.

data.name: DropdownMenuItem — Basic
data.description: Dropdown menu items with labels and secondary descriptions. Use DropdownMenuItem to render custom menu entries with consistent styling.

data.name: Edit form with footer actions
data.description: Compose a Layout with DrawerHeader, the fields in LayoutContent, and Cancel and Save in a pinned LayoutFooter. purpose="form" keeps Escape but ignores scrim clicks, so a stray click outside does not discard edits.

data.name: EmptyState
data.description: A no-results empty state with an icon, descriptive message, and a call-to-action button.

data.name: EmptyState — Actions
data.description: Full empty state with icon, message, and action buttons. Use when a search returns no results, a filter clears all items, or a list has been emptied. The buttons give the user a way forward: go back, clear filters, or try a different query.

data.name: EmptyState — Compact
data.description: Smaller empty state with reduced spacing for constrained areas. Use inside sidebar panels, card widgets, or notification drawers where a full-size empty state would overwhelm the layout.

data.name: EmptyState — Container
data.description: Empty state wrapped in a Card for first-time setup or onboarding. Use when the user has not created any items yet, like a project list, team roster, or dashboard widget that will fill with data once they take action.

data.name: Executive Summary Dashboard
data.description: Report-shaped analytics with a prose rail beside the charts: a scorecard of headline numbers with period deltas and status coloring, goal-attainment bars, a trend grid, and a written commentary column that folds beneath the content when narrow.

data.name: Field
data.description: A form field wrapping a text input with a label, description, and validation status.

data.name: Field — Description
data.description: Fields with helper text below the label. Use descriptions to explain format requirements, constraints, or what happens with the data, like "At least 8 characters" or "We will send a confirmation link".

data.name: Field — Required & Optional
data.description: Required and optional field indicators side by side. Use isRequired on fields the user must fill in, and isOptional to clarify which fields can be skipped.

data.name: Field — Validation States
data.description: All three validation states: error, warning, and success. Use error for invalid input, warning for potential issues like reserved names, and success to confirm valid entries like API keys.

data.description: Standalone labels with required and optional indicators and a helper description. Use when labeling a custom control that does not render its own label.

data.name: FieldStatus — Basic
data.description: Detached error and success messages for validation feedback. Use below checkboxes, switches, or custom controls where an attached status would overlap.

data.name: File Explorer
data.description: Hierarchical browser that drills through nested levels as adjacent columns rather than replacing the list each time, with breadcrumb history, switchable list and grid density, and a metadata pane for the selected node.

data.name: FileInput — Basic
data.description: A controlled single-file upload with accepted types, a size limit, and helper text. Use for standard document upload fields in forms.

data.name: Filterable Table
data.description: Flat row collection built around progressive filtering: a token bar that escalates into full query syntax, saved views that persist a filter set, column and grouping options, and a resizable detail pane.

data.name: Form Wizard
data.description: Linear multi-step form that moves through one panel at a time, with a horizontal progress track pinned above rather than running down a rail, so every step keeps the full content width for its fields. data.name: FormLayout
data.description: A vertical form layout with text input fields.

data.name: FormLayout — Horizontal

data.description: Address form mixing vertical and horizontal layouts for grouped fields

data.name: FormLayout — Settings Form
data.description: Settings form with labels placed beside their inputs

data.name: Gallery Hero
data.description: Centered stack (headline, short blurb, call-to-action buttons) resolving into a multi-image photo grid rather than one wide full-bleed picture, so the imagery reads as a set.

data.description: Card gallery with responsive columns that maintain consistent widths

data.name: Grid — Dashboard Layout
data.description: Dashboard layout with mixed-size widgets and a full-width summary row

data.name: Grid — Responsive Auto-Fit

data.name: Grouped Table
data.description: Row collection bundled into collapsible sections with per-group counts, so a long list reads as a handful of blocks that expand and collapse. Query filtering and a resizable inspector for the selected row.

data.name: Heading — Page Hierarchy

data.name: Heading — Truncation
data.description: Single-line and multi-line heading truncation with ellipsis for constrained layouts

data.name: HoverCard

data.name: HoverCard — Link Preview

data.description: Demonstrates HStack arranging items horizontally with different gaps and alignments.

data.description: Non-semantic color palette for icons.

data.description: All semantic icon color variants with labels.

data.description: All icon sizes from extra-small to large.

data.description: Read-only settings whose labels carry an InfoTip that says who can change each value.

data.description: Override a small number of Astryx strings without providing a full locale catalog.

data.description: Modifier combinations and special keys rendered as shortcut badges

data.name: Layout — Full Bleed Content
data.description: A layout where content extends edge-to-edge with zero padding, ideal for tables or images.

data.name: LayoutFooter — Actions

data.name: LayoutHeader — With Actions

data.name: LayoutPanel — Navigation
data.description: A fixed-width side panel holding a navigation list next to the main content. Use LayoutPanel in the start or end slot of Layout for sidebars.

data.name: Lightbox
data.description: A fullscreen image viewer with caption.

data.name: Lightbox — Gallery

data.description: A single Step, with every part it can render: the indicator, the label with its optional marker and trailing endContent, and the description beneath. In a full flow you gate the slot on the step being active. That is what turns a vertical stepper into an expanding one.

data.name: Step — Indicator
data.description: Everything the indicator prop accepts: the auto default, an always-number badge, a custom ReactNode, and none, each on its own completed Step so the prop is the only difference between them. Every variant occupies the same 16px box, so a step swapping its number for a check as it completes never shifts the label beside it. The last cell shows that a custom node can be live rather than static: a Spinner on a step that is in progress, shaded `inherit` so it picks up the step's own tint like any other glyph.

data.name: Step — States
data.description: Every state a single Step can land in, each shown as one Step in its own Stepper. Completed, current, and upcoming are derived by comparing the step index against the parent activeStep, so they are never set directly; isDisabled and status are the two a step declares itself. Status is a separate axis from progress, which is why a completed step can still carry a warning.

data.name: Stepper — Checkout Progress
data.description: The default stepper: a horizontal track where every step owns an equal segment of the progress bar above its label. The default auto indicator resolves itself per step: a check once the step is done, a ring on the current step, a number for the ones still ahead. Click any step to jump.

data.name: Stepper — Custom Content
data.description: A vertical stepper where each step owns a slice of the page. The content slot takes any node (form fields, a summary panel, a banner), so a stepper is not limited to multi-step forms. Rendering the slot only for the active step is what makes the flow expand one step at a time.

data.name: Stepper — Horizontal Narrow Collapsed

data.name: Stepper — Indicator Modes
data.description: The indicator prop side by side: none (the bar and label carry the progress on their own), auto (check when done, ring when current, number ahead), always-number, and a custom icon per step.

data.name: Stepper — On-Track Horizontal
data.description: The on-track layout in horizontal orientation: instead of sitting beside the label, each indicator is slotted into the connector itself, so the numbered nodes read as beads on one continuous line. Labels center under their node.

data.name: Stepper — On-Track Vertical
data.description: The on-track layout in vertical orientation: indicators sit inline on a continuous connector rail, with each label and description beside its node. Compare with the separated layout, where the indicator sits alongside its own bar segment instead of on a shared rail.

data.name: Stepper — Validation Status
